newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL GOV'T SAYS 25 PCT OF SOYBEAN EXPORTS LEFT.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL GOV'T SAYS 25 PCT OF SOYBEAN EXPORTS LEFT.

text.p: The Brazilian government estimates that 25 percent of the soybean harvest remains to be exported, said Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade at the Ministry of Industry and Commerce.
Cortes told reporters that the coffee industry also planned to export another $1.5 billion before the end of the year.
Cortes said the figures came from a survey of soybean and coffee exporters.
He said that in the January to July period, soybean exports amounted to $4.122 billion.
"The industry says there is still about $1.4 billion to be exported, or something like 25 percent of the harvest," he said.
Exports for the whole of 1997, boosted by international prices for soybean and a record Brazilian harvest, should reach $5.522 billion, up 24.6 percent on 1996, according to Cortes.
Independent consultants Safras e Mercado said last week 92 percent of the 1996/97 soybean harvest had been sold.
Cortes said the survey of coffee exporters revealed that exports in January-July reached $1.597 billion.
"The expectation is that between August and December they will export another $1.595 billion," he said.
Last year, coffee exports amounted to $2.094 billion. This year they are forecast to reach $3.191 billion, Cortes said.
Soybean and coffee exports have been identified as the saviours of Brazil's deteriorating trade balance, running at a deficit of some $5.5 billion so far this year.
But officials have recently been at pains to point out that manufactured exports are also growing.
